# HibbittsDesign.org

> Open-source Docsify and Grav publishing tools that turn Markdown files into websites, from instant single-page publishing to a full flat-file CMS. Built by Paul Hibbitts for educators, digital publishers, and content creators.

All projects are free, open-source, and MIT licensed; none require a database. They form three levels of publishing capability, from least to most setup: publish instantly with Docsify-This, launch a static site with a Docsify Starter Kit, or run a full CMS with Grav – free with Open Publishing Space or Open Course Hub, or with Grav Premium Helios (Open Reader or Course Hub) as a step up. Content in every option stays as plain, portable Markdown files. The site's tagline is "Where Systems-Oriented UX Shapes Open Source" – "Your Markdown, Published Your Way." Paul draws on 25+ years of software interaction design, UX consulting, and university teaching experience; see About Paul below for background and open-source philosophy.

## Main Pages

- [Home](https://hibbittsdesign.org/): Overview of the core projects (Docsify-This, the Docsify Starter Kits, and the free Grav projects with their Grav Premium Helios step ups) and the three-level publishing model, with a live before/after Markdown demo.
- [About Paul](https://hibbittsdesign.org/about.html): Background, teaching history (SFU CMPT-363), the Learning + Technology Development Process Model, and open-source design philosophy.
- [Services](https://hibbittsdesign.org/services.html): Optional paid professional services – workflow/UX optimization, priority support, tutorials and workshops, custom Docsify/Grav development.
- [Testimonials](https://hibbittsdesign.org/testimonials.html): Feedback from educators, publishers, and open-source users of Docsify-This, the Docsify Starter Kits, and the Grav Open Course Hub.
- [Grav CMS Projects at a Glance](https://hibbittsdesign.org/grav-projects-at-a-glance.html): Every Grav project on one map – open guides and books, course sites and documentation, free or Grav Premium Helios – plus the converters that bring content in.
- [Grav Open Publishing Space](https://hibbittsdesign.org/grav-open-publishing-space.html): The free open guide and book site, with a blog and other pages alongside it; its Grav Premium Helios step up is Open Reader.
- [Grav Open Course Hub](https://hibbittsdesign.org/grav-open-course-hub.html): The free course site for one course, with Grav Open MultiCourse Hub for several; its Grav Premium Helios step up is Course Hub.
- [Grav Helios Open Reader](https://hibbittsdesign.org/grav-helios-open-reader.html): The Grav Premium Helios reading site for open textbooks and OER.
- [Grav Helios Course Hub](https://hibbittsdesign.org/grav-helios-course-hub.html): The Grav Premium Helios site for one or several courses.
- [More Cost-Free Grav Projects](https://hibbittsdesign.org/cost-free-grav-projects.html): The free Git Page Link, Mermaid and Admin2 Site ReadMe plugins, and the Learn2 with Git Sync documentation site.
- [Contact](https://hibbittsdesign.org/contact.html): Email address and contact form.

## Projects

- [Docsify-This](https://docsify-this.net/): Instantly turn any online Markdown file, including README files on GitHub or Codeberg, into a shareable, styled web page or embeddable widget – no signup, no build step. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/docsify-this
- [Docsify Starter Kits](https://github.com/hibbitts-design/docsify-open-publishing-starter-kit): Ready-to-use GitHub Pages templates (Open Course Kit, Open MultiCourse Kit, Open Publishing Kit) for a full Markdown-based site with a custom domain and CSS, no build tooling.
- [Grav Open Publishing Space](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-open-publishing-quark2/): Free skeleton for a site with one or several open guides or books, on the Quark 2 theme (Quark in the Grav 1.7 version), with a blog and almost any other Grav page alongside it: section cards, parts, reading progress, Keep My Place, a "This page as Markdown" link on every page and an optional full text version of each guide (llms-full.txt, Grav 2 version), print-friendly pages, and embedding in an LMS with ?embedded=true. Guides can move between it and Grav Helios Open Reader, and Pressbooks books can be imported with the free Pressbooks Converter. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-open-publishing-space
- [Grav Open Course Hub](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-open-course-hub): Free single-course hub skeleton with a Home page of weekly reminders, modules (as in Grav Helios Course Hub), a course blog with tags, archives and RSS that can also hold weekly materials, and course search, in the 2026 Modern style with a tinted NavBar in the course's colour. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-course-hub
- [Grav Open MultiCourse Hub](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-open-multi-course-hub): Free multi-course hub skeleton with a course-selection layer, each course with its own look and organised by modules (with an optional course blog) or by weekly units, in the 2026 Modern style with a tinted NavBar in each course's colour. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-multicourse-hub
- [Grav Helios Open Reader](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-helios-open-reader/): Web-first reader platform for open textbooks and OER (open educational resources), and a web-first alternative to Pressbooks for web reading only (no PDF or EPUB export). Built on Grav and the paid Grav Premium Helios theme. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-helios-open-reader
- [Grav Helios Course Hub](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-helios-course-hub/): Single- or multi-course hub CMS built on Grav and the paid Grav Premium Helios theme, with a browser-based admin panel. Write course content in Markdown and embed it in Canvas, Moodle, or Brightspace (a content layer, not an LMS). Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-helios-course-hub
- [Grav Learn2 with Git Sync](https://demo.hibbittsdesign.org/grav-learn2-git-sync/): Free documentation-site skeleton with search and RSS/Atom feeds. Source: https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-skeleton-learn2-with-git-sync
- [Git Page Link Plugin](https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-plugin-git-page-link): Free plugin that adds an "Edit this Page" link back to the Markdown source, works with most Grav themes.
- [Mermaid Plugin](https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-plugin-mermaid): Free plugin that draws Mermaid diagrams (flowcharts, timelines, sequence diagrams and more) from text in a page, in light or dark mode to match the theme, with titles and descriptions for screen readers; works with most Grav themes, on Grav 2 and 1.7.
- [Admin2 Site ReadMe Plugin](https://github.com/hibbitts-design/grav-plugin-admin2-site-readme): Free Grav 2 plugin that shows a site's own ReadMe, such as a README on GitHub, in the Admin 2 sidebar, so the people editing a site can read its how-tos where they work.

## Import & Conversion Tools

Free, ongoing-beta converters for bringing existing course or book content into these tools. Each handles the common cases well but isn't a guaranteed complete migration.

- [Docsify Cartridge Converter](https://docsify-common-cartridge-converter.hibbittsdesign.org/): Imports a Canvas, Moodle, or Brightspace Common Cartridge export into a ready-to-edit Docsify site, for use with either Docsify-This or the Docsify Starter Kits. Source: https://github.com/paulhibbitts/docsify-common-cartridge-converter
- [Pressbooks Converter](https://pressbooks-converter.hibbittsdesign.org/): Imports existing Pressbooks content into the free Grav Open Publishing Space or Grav Helios Open Reader. Source: https://github.com/paulhibbitts/grav-helios-pressbooks-converter
- [Common Cartridge Converter](https://common-cartridge-converter.hibbittsdesign.org/): The same Common Cartridge import, for Grav Open Course Hub (as a Modules section), Grav Open MultiCourse Hub, or Grav Helios Course Hub. Source: https://github.com/paulhibbitts/grav-helios-common-cartridge-converter

## Articles

- [Systems-Oriented Design in Practice: The Structure Beneath the Surface](https://hibbittsdesign.org/systems-oriented-design.html): Paul's systems-oriented design approach, illustrated through structural and architectural lessons from building Docsify-This and the Grav Helios Course Hub.
- [Building Open Source Projects with a Positive Vibe: 8 Practical Guidelines](https://hibbittsdesign.org/open-source-with-a-positive-vibe.html): Paul's philosophy on fostering emotional connection and community in open-source projects, developed while building Docsify-This.
- [A Dual-Purpose Framework for Better Open Source Documentation](https://hibbittsdesign.org/dual-purpose-documentation-framework.html): A three-part documentation framework (problem/solution, design principles, good-fit vs. not-a-good-fit) that doubles as a development compass.
